Subject: Request: pseudonymization tiering + cross-border subprocessor evidence

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. Synapse is close to finalizing our internal security signoff but we need a short evidence pack to close two items: 1) confirmation of where PII is pseudonymized or tokenized (tiering by field) prior to any cross-border transfer, and 2) a list of subprocessors and the country/region where each processes the raw data.

Specific asks:
- A dataflow diagram that highlights the point(s) where pseudonymization occurs (we want a V2 if possible).
- A CSV with each PII field name, pseudonymization method (hashing, tokenization, redaction), and whether raw plaintext ever leaves the processing region.
- Which subprocessors may receive telemetry/observability artifacts and whether telemetry is truncated/aggregated before egress.
- Any attestation we can rely on for KMS custody (who holds key material and whether any subprocessor can decrypt).

Can you provide something by EOD Tue 16 Jun? If some items require legal review (DPA Annex text), flag that and we can accept a staged delivery.

Best,
Ravi Patel
Privacy Ops (Synapse Health)
privacy_ops@synapsehealth.com

Hi Ravi — thanks for the clear list. We're putting together an evidence bundle; preliminary answers inline and an initial artifact drop attached.

Quick summary:
- Dataflow diagram: attached redwood-dataflow-v2.svg (annotated). It marks pseudonymization gates and telemetry sinks.
- Field mapping: attached pseudonymization-index.csv — each row is a field, method, and processing zone.
- Subprocessors & endpoints: we'll send a dedicated CSV from CS with IP/region mapping (sends next).
- Telemetry: we perform telemetry minimization. Application-level telemetry is truncated at the proxy layer before it crosses regions (details in CSV).
- KMS custody: Redwood holds the primary tenant key in an HSM-backed KMS. Subprocessor access is via a short-lived, audited proxy; no subprocessor has persistent key material to decrypt tenant data. Connor is looping in legal for a short attestation language for the DPA Annex.

Attached: redwood-dataflow-v2.svg (SVG), pseudonymization-index.csv (CSV).

Next steps (our side):
- Marissa will attach the subprocessor endpoint roster (with region) in a follow-up.
- Connor to provide suggested Annex wording and attestations.

Deliverable timeline: we can get the endpoint roster and Connor's draft by tomorrow (16 Jun) EOD. If you need a formal signed attestation, please indicate and we'll route to Legal + Security SLA team.

Thanks,

Ravi / team — attaching the subprocessor endpoint roster you asked for. Notes below.

What I attached: subprocessor-endpoints.csv — columns: subprocessor_name, service_role, processing_region, endpoint_hostname, raw_plaintext_access (yes/no), telemetry_received (full/min/trunc).

Key clarifications:
- Three subprocessors perform regional batch indexing (EU, US, APAC). They receive only pseudonymized identifiers; raw plaintext fields are never forwarded to those endpoints.
- Our logging/observability pipeline receives event slices but we truncate message and prompt content at the proxy. Truncation removes any token-level content beyond token N and strips high-entropy segments by hashing.
- There is a small engineering fallback used for model debugging where encrypted snapshots (customer-consented, time-limited) can be pulled into an internal debugging enclave; access is strictly limited and audited. We marked those rows in the CSV as "enclave-access: yes" and included justification notes.

Attachments: subprocessor-endpoints.csv

Let me know if you want a redline of the Annex language or a short timeline for an attestation letter.

Cheers,

Thanks — this is very helpful. Two follow-ups before we mark as resolved:
1) KMS attestation: can you confirm in a single sentence whether any named subprocessor can decrypt tenant data without Redwood-issued short-lived credentials? We need a yes/no and a one-line explanation for our compliance team.
2) Quantitative truncation: you mention token truncation at the proxy. Can you provide the truncation policy (e.g., first 128 tokens kept, remainder hashed) or a pointer to a policy doc? A short text file is fine.

If you can provide those two items by EOD 16 Jun we can close the SSQ and move to legal DPA review. If legal redlines are expected, please attach drafts.

Subject: Re: Request: pseudonymization tiering + cross-border subprocessor evidence

Ravi — final answers and attachments below. I've forwarded Connor's suggested DPA Annex text at the bottom.

Quick KMS attestation (one-liner): No subprocessor can decrypt tenant data without a Redwood-issued short-lived credential or an explicit, auditable key-release event; Redwood's HSM-backed KMS holds the root tenant key material and subprocessors access data only via ephemeral proxies.

Truncation policy (summary):
- Proxy truncation rule: keep first 128 tokens of a user prompt/response, replace subsequent tokens with a 256-bit SHA-256 hash; high-entropy fields (SSNs, full credit card numbers) are detected by regex and redacted completely before truncation.
- Telemetry aggregation: request IDs are hashed; sampling set for full-stack traces is 0.5% by default and limited to internal debugging enclaves (with access controls).

Attached artifacts:
- dpa-annex1-redline.docx (Connor's suggested wording for Annex 1: KMS custody, subprocessor carveouts, and attestation language)
- redwood-dataflow-v2.svg (updated with labels for truncation gates)
- pseudonymization-index.csv (finalized with enclave-access flags)

Forwarded for legal:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-16T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: DPA Annex 1 draft

Olga — below is the DPA Annex wording I recommend sending as a base to the customer; it's intentionally narrow and attestation-based: 

"Redwood Inference confirms that tenant data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific keys stored in an HSM-backed KMS under Redwood custody. Subprocessors do not hold persistent key material; any decryption activity required for troubleshooting is performed via a time-limited, auditable key-release controlled by Redwood and recorded in audit logs. Redwood will provide a signed attestation upon request, limited to the scope of the relevant tenant and time period."

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
